label: Claude Code
hint: The official installer writes it to the PATH.

desktop.label: Claude Desktop
desktop.note: Claude Desktop is a different product with a configuration file of its own, and a terminal cannot run it.

label: OpenCode
hint: It installs through npm, Homebrew, or Scoop.

label: OpenAI Codex CLI
hint: It installs through npm or Homebrew.

desktop.label: the ChatGPT desktop application
desktop.note: The ChatGPT desktop application reads the same .codex/config.toml file, so a server registered here reaches it too. A terminal cannot run it.

label: Antigravity CLI
hint: Google ships it as the follower of Gemini CLI.

desktop.label: the Antigravity editor
desktop.note: The Antigravity editor reads the same mcp_config.json file, so a server registered here reaches it too. A terminal cannot run it.

label: Gemini CLI
hint: It installs through npm. Google ended the consumer tiers on 2026-06-18.

label: GitHub Copilot CLI
hint: It installs through npm or winget, and it needs a Copilot subscription.

label: Cursor CLI
hint: The Cursor installer writes both names to the PATH.

desktop.label: the Cursor editor
desktop.note: The Cursor editor reads the same mcp.json file, so a server registered here reaches it too. A terminal cannot run it.

label: Aider
hint: It installs through pip or pipx. It reads no Model Context Protocol server.

label: Amp
hint: Sourcegraph ships it, and it needs a paid plan.

desktop.label: Amp for macOS
desktop.note: Amp for macOS is a separate application, and a terminal cannot run it.

label: Another agent
hint: Name the command yourself. A shell function works, because a shell runs the command.

label: No agent
hint: The window starts nothing. Copy the tasks and paste them where your agent runs.
